newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian official says Malaysia "paid" for Games.
newsitem.headline: Australian official says Malaysia "paid" for Games.

text.p: A leading Australian sports official said Malaysia had won the right to host the 1998 Commonwealth Games through "the power of money", Australian media reported on Saturday.

Controversial Australian Commonwealth Games official Arthur Tunstall reportedly told a sports gathering in South Australia state on Thursday that Adelaide, which unsuccessfully bid against Kuala Lumpur, could not match "what was being bought".
"It was unfortunate the power of money and other influences won the day," Saturday's Sydney Morning Herald quoted Tunstall as saying.

"I've got a fair idea what went on but I'm not prepared to talk about how much money or anything else was given but yes, it was more than a T-shirt," the Australian Commonwealth Games Association secretary-general said.
Contacted after his address to the South Australian Olympic Council on Thursday, Tunstall told Adelaide's The Advertiser newspaper that Kuala Lumpur had done nothing wrong.

The Sydney Morning Herald said that, while there was no official comment from Malaysia, Games organisers were believed to be sending copies of Tunstall's comments to Commonwealth Games Federation chairman Michael Fennell.
Tunstall was forced to apologise two years ago for telling a perceived racist joke about Australian sprinter Cathy Freeman and another Aboriginal athlete.
Tunstall had also criticised Freeman for carrying an Aboriginal flag after winning a race at the Commonwealth Games in Canada in 1994.
